answer: Randomized Enrollment Terracing. Each epoch, a verifiable random beacon assigns new agents to fixed-capacity slots on a registration terrace; only slots opened by the beacon can enroll, and identities failing to hold a slot across a lotus-shaped rotation window are dropped. An attacker cannot precompute slot openings, so mass pre-registration fails. Each surviving identity must pay an ivory-priced renewal bound to its slot, making N clones cost N beacon-timed renewals rather than one bulk fee.
